paragraphs: On Thursday, the school cafeteria was busy at lunch. Lily, Mia, Leo, and May stood in the line with their trays. A big board above the counter showed the food of the day. It said, "MUSHROOM SOUP, FRIED RICE, MELON." "Let's all have the soup," said May. "It is hot, and it smells good."

"I think I prefer the fried rice," said Leo. "I am very hungry, and the rice is big." "Shall we share the melon?" asked Mia. "One slice for each of us is enough." "Good idea, because the melon is fresh and cold," said Lily. They took four slices of melon and a bottle of cold juice. Leo took the fried rice, and the other three took the soup and a piece of bread.

They sat at a long table near the window, and the sun was warm on their trays. The soup was hot, and the mushrooms were soft. Lily opened her notebook next to her tray. "Teacher Kim says that we need a new post for the blog," she said. "Let's write about food, because everybody likes lunch." "We can call it Food Week," said May. "Why not make a plan for five days?" "Each day, we write about one dish, and we add a photo from the cafeteria."

"I think that we start with today's soup," said Mia. "It is easy to describe, and the mushrooms are very good." "My aunt lives in the capital," she said. "She says that the department store there has a big food hall with food from many countries." "We cannot go there, but we can ask her for a photo," said Lily. "Shall I write the email?" asked May. "Yes, please," said Mia.

"What will I do?" asked Leo with his mouth full. "You can draw a cartoon of a hungry melon," said Lily. "That is a funny idea, so I will do it," said Leo. "The melon will say please eat me, and a big knife will come," he added. Everybody laughed, and Mia nearly dropped her bread.

When lunch was over, the four friends carried their trays to the counter. A cook gave them a big smile and said, "Thank you for the empty plates." "Let's meet in the library at the club hour," said Lily. "We can write the first line of Food Week there." She closed her notebook and wrote one word on the cover: "Food."
text.summary: At lunch in the school cafeteria, Lily, Mia, Leo, and May choose their food and make suggestions for a blog post called "Food Week."

sentences.text: On Thursday, the school cafeteria was busy at lunch.
Lily, Mia, Leo, and May stood in the line with their trays.
A big board above the counter showed the food of the day.
It said, "MUSHROOM SOUP, FRIED RICE, MELON."
"Let's all have the soup," said May.
"It is hot, and it smells good."
"I think I prefer the fried rice," said Leo.
"I am very hungry, and the rice is big."
"Shall we share the melon?" asked Mia.
"One slice for each of us is enough."
"Good idea, because the melon is fresh and cold," said Lily.
They took four slices of melon and a bottle of cold juice.
Leo took the fried rice, and the other three took the soup and a piece of bread.
They sat at a long table near the window, and the sun was warm on their trays.
The soup was hot, and the mushrooms were soft.
Lily opened her notebook next to her tray.
"Teacher Kim says that we need a new post for the blog," she said.
"Let's write about food, because everybody likes lunch."
"We can call it Food Week," said May.
"Why not make a plan for five days?"
"Each day, we write about one dish, and we add a photo from the cafeteria."
"I think that we start with today's soup," said Mia.
"It is easy to describe, and the mushrooms are very good."
"My aunt lives in the capital," she said.
"She says that the department store there has a big food hall with food from many countries."
"We cannot go there, but we can ask her for a photo," said Lily.
"Shall I write the email?" asked May.
"Yes, please," said Mia.
"What will I do?" asked Leo with his mouth full.
"You can draw a cartoon of a hungry melon," said Lily.
"That is a funny idea, so I will do it," said Leo.
"The melon will say please eat me, and a big knife will come," he added.
Everybody laughed, and Mia nearly dropped her bread.
When lunch was over, the four friends carried their trays to the counter.
A cook gave them a big smile and said, "Thank you for the empty plates."
"Let's meet in the library at the club hour," said Lily.
"We can write the first line of Food Week there."
She closed her notebook and wrote one word on the cover: "Food."
